sources.title: Fossil hunting: How to find fossils on the beach

facts.statement: Fosil, çok eski canlıların korunmuş kalıntısı ya da kalıntı izidir.
facts.quote: Fossils are the preserved remains, or traces of remains, of ancient organisms.
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Fossil

facts.statement: Fosil kelimesi Latince 'fossilis'ten gelir; 'kazılıp çıkarılmış' demektir.
facts.quote: The word fossil is derived from the Latin fossilis meaning ‘unearthed’.
facts.location: British Geological Survey — Fossils

facts.statement: Korunmuş kalıntılar 10.000 yıldan yaşlıysa fosil sayılır; fosiller tipik olarak 10.000 yıldan eskidir.
facts.quote: Preserved remains are defined as fossils if they are older than 10,000 years old. / Fossils also include any preserved trace of life that is typically more than 10 000 years old.
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Fossil; British Geological Survey — Fossils

facts.statement: Vücut fosilleri kemik, diş, deri, kabuk, odun ve yaprakları kapsar.
facts.quote: Body fossils include bones, teeth, skin, shells, wood, and leaves.
facts.location: U.S. National Park Service — What is a Fossil?

facts.statement: İz fosilleri, canlının yaşarken yaptığı etkinlikten kalır: ayak izleri, yuva tünelleri, koprolitler gibi.
facts.quote: Trace fossils result from activity of an organism while it is alive. / Trace fossils include footprints, tracks, burrows, trails, coprolites, root traces,
facts.location: U.S. National Park Service — What is a Fossil?

facts.statement: İz fosilleri, başka türlü bilinemeyecek davranış bilgilerini ortaya çıkarır.
facts.quote: trace fossils reveal information about behavior that would not otherwise be known.
facts.location: U.S. National Park Service — What is a Fossil?

facts.statement: Koprolit, milyonlarca yıl önce yaşamış hayvanların fosilleşmiş dışkısıdır; bir iz fosilidir.
facts.quote: Coprolites are the fossilised faeces of animals that lived millions of years ago. / They’re trace fossils, meaning not of the animal’s actual body.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — What is a coprolite?

facts.statement: Koprolitte kemik parçaları varsa hayvan etçildi; tohum, yaprak kalıntısı, polen ya da kabuk varsa bitki yiyordu.
facts.quote: If there are bone fragments, the animal was a carnivore. / Seeds, leaf remains, pollen or bark found in a coprolite suggest that the animal it came from ate plants.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — What is a coprolite?

facts.statement: Hayvan ölür; deri ve kas gibi yumuşak kısımlar çürümeye başlar; tamamen yok olmadan çamur, kum ya da siltle örtülür; çoğu zaman yalnızca kemikler ve dişler kalır.
facts.quote: The animal dies. / Soft parts of the animal's body, including skin and muscles, start to rot away. / Before the body disappears completely, it is buried by sediment - usually mud, sand or silt. / Often at this point only the bones and teeth remain.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?

facts.statement: Hızlı gömülme fosilleşme için gereklidir; ölümden kısa süre sonra tortuyla örtülmek kalıntıyı çürümekten ve aşınmaktan korur.
facts.quote: Rapid burial by sediments that were previously suspended in water is required for fossilisation to occur. / Burial by sediment soon after an organism dies prevents the remains from decomposition, weathering
facts.location: British Geological Survey — Fossils; U.S. National Park Service — How Fossils Form

facts.statement: Üstüne çok sayıda tortu katmanı birikir; bunlar zamanla tortul kayaya dönüşür.
facts.quote: Many more layers of sediment build up on top. / Eventually, they turn into sedimentary rock.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?

facts.statement: Su kemiklere ve dişlere sızar, geride mineral bırakarak onları taşa çevirir; permineralizasyon, organik maddedeki minik gözeneklerin dolmasıdır.
facts.quote: While this is happening, water seeps into the bones and teeth, turning them to stone as it leaves behind minerals. / Permineralization is the infilling of tiny pores in organic material.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?; U.S. National Park Service — What is a Fossil?

facts.statement: Bu süreç binlerce, hatta milyonlarca yıl sürebilir.
facts.quote: This process can take thousands or even millions of years.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?

facts.statement: Yeraltı suyu gömülü kemiği ya da kabuğu çözerse onun biçiminde bir boşluk (kalıp) kalır; mineralli su bu boşluğu doldurursa aynı biçimde bir fosil (döküm) oluşur.
facts.quote: Sometimes ground water dissolves the buried bone or shell, leaving behind a bone- or shell-shaped hole / If water rich in minerals fills this space, crystals can form and create a fossil in the shape / it may leave behind a space in the shape of the original material called a mould. / A cast is a positive impression of the original material formed by contact with the mould.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?; British Geological Survey — Fossils

facts.statement: Ağaçların yapışkan reçinesi fosilleşebilir (kehribar); kehribar karınca, sinek gibi narin canlıların bedenlerini koruyabilir.
facts.quote: Sometimes, however, the sticky resin of a tree can become fossilized. / Amber can preserve the bodies of many delicate, soft-bodied organisms, such as ants, flies, and mosquitoes.
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Fossil

facts.statement: Fosilleşme çok nadir bir olaydır; ölen canlıların çoğu tamamen çürür ve geriye bir şey kalmaz.
facts.quote: A specific set of circumstances and conditions are needed for fossilisation to occur, so it is actually a very rare event. / Most things that die rot away completely, leaving nothing behind.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?

facts.statement: Fosilleşme, iskelet, diş, kabuk gibi sert parçaları olan canlılarda daha sık görülür; solucan gibi yumuşak gövdeli canlılar nadiren fosilleşir.
facts.quote: Fossilization more commonly occurs in organisms with hard, bony body parts, such as skeletons, teeth, or shells. / Soft-bodied organisms, such as worms, are rarely fossilized, because soft parts quickly decompose or are eaten.
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Fossil

facts.statement: Bulunan fosillerin neredeyse tamamı, yaklaşık %99'u, kabuklular ve köpek balıkları gibi deniz hayvanlarına aittir.
facts.quote: Nearly all fossils we find - around 99% - are from marine animals such as shellfish and sharks.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?

facts.statement: Fosiller, oluşma biçimleri nedeniyle tortul kayalarda bulunur.
facts.quote: Because of how they form, fossils occur in sedimentary rocks.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?

facts.statement: Rüzgâr, yağmur, buz, sıcaklık ve nehirlerin yol açtığı aşınma kayaları parçalar; fosiller yavaş yavaş yüzeye çıkar.
facts.quote: Weathering and erosion from wind, rain, ice, heat and rivers break rocks apart / It can take millions of years, but gradually fossils become exposed at the surface where we can find them.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?

facts.statement: Deniz hayvanlarının fosilleri Everest'in tepesinde bulunabilir; Himalayaları oluşturan kayalar bir zamanlar okyanusun dibindeydi.
facts.quote: This is why fossils of marine animals can be found at the top of Mount Everest. / the rocks that became the Himalayas were at the bottom of the ocean.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — How are dinosaur fossils formed?; National Geographic Education — Fossil

facts.statement: Paleontologlar fosilleri inceleyen kişilerdir; fosiller türlerin nasıl yaşadığını ve Dünya'nın nasıl değiştiğini öğrenmeye yardım eder.
facts.quote: Paleontologists are people who study fossils. / Studying fossils helps them learn about when and how different species lived millions of years ago. / Sometimes, fossils tell scientists how the Earth has changed.
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Fossil

facts.statement: En eski fosiller neredeyse 4 milyar yaşındadır ve okyanusta yaşamış bakterilerin izleridir.
facts.quote: The oldest fossils are almost 4 billion years old and are traces of ocean-dwelling bacteria.
facts.location: National Geographic Education — Fossil

facts.statement: ABD Ulusal Park Sistemi'nin bütün birimlerinde fosil toplamak yasaktır; tek bir fosil, bütün bir türün var olduğunun tek kanıtı olabilir.
facts.quote: collecting fossils for recreational, commercial, or educational use is prohibited in all units of the National Park System / A single fossil may be the only evidence of the existence of an entire species.
facts.location: U.S. National Park Service — Visit Park Fossils

facts.statement: Bazı yerlerde bakılabilir ama hiçbir şey toplanamaz; önemli olabilecek bir fosil görülürse bir müzeye bildirilmesi önerilir.
facts.quote: In some places you can look but mustn’t collect anything. / If you spot a fossil that you think may be exciting or important, report it to a Museum
facts.location: Natural History Museum — Fossil hunting: How to find fossils on the beach

facts.statement: Köpek balığı dişleri, en bol bulunan omurgalı fosilleridir.
facts.quote: Shark teeth are the most abundant vertebrate fossils.
facts.location: Natural History Museum — What is a fossil?
